issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s right to seek immediate possession accrues when an ownership-based order requiring the landlord to vacate government accommodation is served, and retirement before filing the eviction application does not defeat that accrued right.
material_facts: The landlord occupied residential accommodation allotted by the government and owned a residential house in the relevant territory.

Before retiring, the landlord was served with a general order requiring him to vacate the allotted accommodation, or otherwise incur an enhanced licence-fee obligation, because he owned a house there.
The landlord retired before filing an eviction application under the newly introduced immediate-possession procedure.
The High Court held that retirement before the eviction application made the special procedure unavailable; the Supreme Court considered the appeal from that ruling.
issues.conclusion: The landlord could invoke the immediate-possession provision notwithstanding his retirement before filing, because the ownership-based order had been served before his retirement and the right accrued on service of that order. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the Rent Controller’s eviction order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14A(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a landlord in occupation of government-allotted residential accommodation who is required by a general or special order to vacate, or otherwise incur an obligation, on the ground that the landlord owns residential accommodation in the territory acquires the right to recover immediate possession on or from the date of that order. Section 25B provided the speedy procedure for pursuing that right; its later availability did not change when the cause of action accrued. The court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: eviction_case_under_special_immediate_possession_procedure and landlord_occupies_government_allotted_residence and landlord_owns_residence_in_relevant_territory and ownership_based_vacate_order_served and order_served_before_retirement and landlord_retired_before_eviction_filing and remedy_available_after_trigger_order

predicates.eviction_case_under_special_immediate_po: The landlord brought an eviction proceeding using a special procedure for seeking immediate possession.
predicates.landlord_occupies_government_allotted_re: The landlord occupied residential accommodation allotted by the government or a local authority.
predicates.landlord_owns_residence_in_relevant_terr: The landlord owned residential accommodation in the territory covered by the special provision.
predicates.ownership_based_vacate_order_served: The landlord was served with an order requiring vacation of the allotted accommodation, or imposing an alternative obligation, because of that ownership.
predicates.order_served_before_retirement: The ownership-based order was served before the landlord retired from service.
predicates.landlord_retired_before_eviction_filing: The landlord retired before filing the eviction application.
predicates.remedy_available_after_trigger_order: The special procedure for pursuing immediate possession became available after the ownership-based order was served.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings the specified eviction proceeding, occupies government-allotted housing, owns a residence in the relevant territory, receives an ownership-based vacate order before retirement, retires before filing, and the special procedure becomes available after the order, the landlord may seek immediate possession.
